notes: 22 new products (zw-201 to zw-222) from Nestlé USA (Hot Pockets 3, Lean Cuisine 2, Stouffer's 2), Kraft Heinz (Velveeta, Kraft, Smart Ones), General Mills (Annie's 2), Hormel Foods (Compleats, Dinty Moore), Campbell's 2, Amy's 2, Tyson Foods (Jimmy Dean 2, Tyson Any'tizers) and Ruiz Foods (El Monterey). None repeat the existing 33.

Hot Pockets crisping sleeve: Nestlé removed the sleeve from Hot Pockets packaging (announced Sept 30, 2024) and moved from 2-packs to 4-packs in 2025. The two 'sleeve' records (zw-201 pepperoni, zw-202 ham & cheddar) come from older 2-pack listings on Uber Eats store pages whose label text still says 'load into crisping sleeve' and 'do not use crisping sleeve in oven/air fryer'. Current boxes (zw-203, and the Hannaford 4-ct croissant-crust listing) say to use a microwave-safe plate, and the ACME carton text reads 'Peace out sleeves!'. The app should treat a Hot Pockets box as sleeveless unless a sleeve is in the box.

Proposed schema additions, used only where needed: category 'plate' for products heated unwrapped on a user-supplied plate or paper towel (zw-203 sleeveless Hot Pockets, zw-219 Jimmy Dean Delights, zw-220 El Monterey burritos, zw-221 Tyson Any'tizers), since none of the existing categories fits; optional fields 'sleeve_label_text', 'quantity_variants' (time by piece count), 'alternate_microwave_method', 'subtype' and 'retailer_item_id'. Remap 'plate' if the app's enum must stay fixed.

Stouffer's French Bread Deluxe (zw-207) is filed as oven_only with subtype 'micro-bake': the label's methods start with a microwave step on a plate but finish in a 425°F oven or 300°F air fryer, with no microwave-only option. Useful as a case where the app must say an oven is required.

Skipped on purpose: Chef Boyardee and Evol are Conagra brands (Chef Boyardee is already on the labelinsight SmartLabel host used for zw-022), so they were left for a Conagra batch. Sweet Earth appears inactive: VegNews (Oct 10, 2026) reports the website redirects to Nestlé and the brand looks discontinued (https://vegnews.com/what-happened-to-sweet-earth-vegan-at-nestle). Saffron Road was not added because the shared web-search quota ran out before a source page was found.

Sources that worked this time: www.hannaford.com product pages (full label transcriptions; the bare hannaford.com host showed a maintenance page and preview.hannaford.com is now robots-disallowed), goodnes.com product and FAQ pages for Nestlé brands, Uber Eats store item pages (directions text, sometimes from older packages), Campbell's Foodservice, foodlion.com (www), tyson.com (no microwave times), the Jimmy Dean Salsify brand page (GTIN only) and acmestores.com (GTIN plus some carton text, no directions). Stop & Shop was in maintenance; curl to heb.com and hannaford.com is blocked by the proxy.

Completeness: 10 complete, 12 partial. Partial records mostly lack a reference wattage (cups, Campbell's bowls, Amy's, Hormel shelf-stable trays). Lean Cuisine reference wattage (1100 W) comes from the brand FAQ because the product pages omit it or show the typo '110 watts'.

UPCs found for 3 products only (zw-203 Hot Pockets 4 Pack GTIN from ACME, zw-214 Campbell's Chili Mac 11-digit form, zw-218 Jimmy Dean bowl GTIN from Salsify). Retailer IDs are kept in retailer_item_id. All need checking against the package barcode.

No resin identification code, and no product-level BPA statement, was found for any tray, cup or bowl in this batch. Container material is stated only at brand level (Lean Cuisine and Stouffer's FAQs) or in news coverage (Kraft fiber cup trial, Nissin paper cup). No Maruchan, Amy's or Hormel corporate packaging statement was found before the search quota ran out.

Power-level cases worth testing in the app: Stouffer's lasagna (HIGH then 50%), Amy's enchilada (MEDIUM then HIGH), Jimmy Dean Delights (30% defrost then HIGH). Explicit low-wattage times appear only on Hot Pockets ('lower wattage/compact microwave' row with no watt number).

Label oddities: Campbell's Chunky Meat Lovers Mac bowl warns 'Metal edges are sharp' and 'Do not reuse or reheat bowl'; Velveeta and Kraft cups warn to add water to the fill line to help prevent fire and not to leave the microwave unattended; Velveeta notes a starch blend in the cup reduces boil-over.

packaging_statements.statement: FAQ, 'Is the tray recyclable?': 'Plastic Trays: Check with your local recycling program to confirm if these trays are accepted.' 'Paperboard: The paperboard outer carton is recyclable.' 'Can I reuse the tray?': 'We do not recommend that the trays be reused. They were not designed as reusable containers.' Preparation: entrée cooking times 'are based on the usage of an 1100-watt microwave oven.'

Development mirror of the same FAQ (02dev host) says: 'Our trays now contain 25% recycled plastic, making them easier to recycle.' and 'LEAN CUISINE does not use BPA when creating our trays.' These lines are not on the production page, so treat them as unconfirmed.

FAQ: plastic trays 'are designed and tested to be safe for cooking food' and 'meet all applicable FDA standards for food contact materials' (BPA not addressed directly). 'Our trays now contain 25% recycled plastic and no longer use black pigment, making them easier to recycle.' Aluminum trays: 'recyclable where suitable recycling programs exist.' 'Our single-serve trays have changed from a plastic tray to a paper tray to cut down on plastic usage by 90%.' 'the pressed paper trays used in our multi-serve meals and select single-serve meals are not yet recyclable.' 'The tray should not be reused.' Film: make two or three small slits; an unvented film 'in a microwave, can balloon and burst.'

FAQ (still references the sleeve): 'We do not recommend that the HOT POCKETS® sleeve be reused. It is intended for single use only.' Oven: 'Please do not use the crisping sleeve in the oven.' Recycling: check packaging labels and local recycling company. FAQ also says 2-packs were replaced by 4-packs, with most stores having the new packs by July 2025.

Packaging Dive (Oct 4, 2024): Hot Pockets removed the microwave susceptor crisping sleeves from its packaging (announced Sept 30, 2024), avoiding more than 6.6 million pounds of packaging material a year including 5 million pounds of paper, and said the change also shortens cook time. Brand quote: 'without the crisping "sleeve" and without sacrificing the crispiness factor'.
Current carton text on ACME listing: 'Peace out sleeves!', tastes great 'without the nuisance of a sleeve', 'Dispose responsibly.'

PlasticsToday (Feb 5, 2021): Kraft Mac & Cheese was testing a 'recyclable, fiber-based, microwavable cup' intended to be 'both recyclable and compostable in industrial composting facilities'; 'The cup currently being trialed is microwave safe.' Liner polymer not disclosed ('cup and design are still being trialed'). The article does not say what the existing cups are made of. The Kraft Heinz investor-relations release on this now returns 404.

2026 Goals and Performance (FY2025): 'Transition 100% of packaging to recyclable or industrially compostable designs and materials by CY2030', reported at 95% progress. No mention of microwavable bowls, polypropylene or BPA.

Green Century shareholder press release (July 14, 2026): Campbell's sells food in plastic packaging labeled 'microwavable' and agreed to disclose its plastic footprint; no resin types given. It questions whether 'recyclable designs' are recyclable in practice under FTC Green Guides.

Walmart listing titles describe Compleats as 'Shelf Stable 9 oz Plastic Tray' and '9 oz Plastic Microwaveable Tray'. Seen only as search-result titles (Walmart pages are not readable); no resin or BPA statement found from Hormel.

FOX 11 Los Angeles (Nov 2, 2023): Nissin announced a new paper cup for early 2024 to 'replace the current polystyrene cup', which 'makes the ramen noodles microwavable in the package.' Liner and recyclability not stated.
